narrative.what_i_did: Migrated tapit-wallet to comms v2 in one commit (004e47d): deleted the five old comms files (appcommander/comms/current.json + interactions.jsonl + in-flight.jsonl + carpenter-opinions.md, appcommander/foreman-context/carpenter-state-for-foreman.md) via git rm; created .carpenter/ at the repo root with a .carpenter/archive/ subfolder (both tracked via .gitkeep); wrote .carpenter/session.json as the single canonical comms file; wrote .claude/hooks/session-close.sh (Stop/PreCompact hook) and .claude/hooks/session-start.sh (SessionStart hook), both chmod +x; merged the new hook entries into the existing .claude/settings.json without overwriting the three pre-existing entries (scripts/session-start-grounding.mjs, the UserPromptSubmit grounding gate, scripts/session-stop-gate.mjs); added a new PreCompact block carrying only the new session-close.sh. After the migration commit landed and was pushed to main, the comms-v2 session-close.sh hook auto-fired on every Stop event, creating checkpoint commits 910d94f and a6d6182 and 4a400da — but its built-in 'git push origin main' line silently failed under this repo's dispatch-sandbox execution mode (PFOR-016 doctrine says the carpenter works on a dispatch branch and pushes to main via 'git push origin <branch>:main' rather than ever checking out a local main snapshot). The old scripts/session-stop-gate.mjs then blocked Stop on each unpushed-commit accumulation, producing an infinite Stop-fire loop. Patched .claude/hooks/session-close.sh to detect the current branch and use the dispatch-branch refspec (<branch>:main) when not on main, with a follow-up push of the branch ref itself so origin tracks the carpenter's working state; the fix preserves the operator's original direct-main behavior on carpenters that work on main directly while making the hook actually complete the loop under sandbox mode. Push of this patch + session.json update is the second commit of this session.
narrative.whats_pending: Three follow-up items the migration did NOT touch and one operator-decision item surfaced by the loop failure. First, CLAUDE.md still extensively documents the retired five-file comms protocol and the closed-loop CARPENTER_HANDOFF.md hand-off; that doctrine block should be rewritten to describe the comms v2 .carpenter/session.json loop instead. Second, scripts/session-start-grounding.mjs (reads CARPENTER_HANDOFF.md from origin/main + injects as additionalContext) and scripts/session-stop-gate.mjs (blocks Stop when commits are ahead of origin/main) are still wired in settings.json alongside the new bash hooks; both implement the old doctrine and are good candidates for retirement now that comms v2 is observed working in sandbox mode. Third, CARPENTER_HANDOFF.md still lives at the repo root carrying the prior session's letter; under comms v2 it is structurally superseded by .carpenter/session.json and is a candidate for removal in a follow-up cut. New surfaced item: the session-close hook now creates a new archive checkpoint commit on every Stop event, even when session.json itself has not changed, because the archive file's timestamp name guarantees a non-empty index diff per invocation; this produces one commit per Stop on the operator's history, which is honest but spammy. Operator may want to add an idempotency check (skip archive when latest archive content hash matches the current session.json) or accept the spam as the cost of guaranteed loop closure.
narrative.what_you_could_do_better: Operator to confirm the session-close hook patch actually clears the Stop-fire infinite loop end-to-end in this environment. The hook was patched, the patch syntax checks, and the dispatch-branch refspec mirrors what the manual workaround used successfully — but the only true test is the next Stop event firing cleanly. If the gate still blocks after this commit pushes, the diagnosis is that the dispatch branch detection failed (git rev-parse fell through to 'main' default) and the operator should check the hook's error stream.
narrative.bigger_picture: Part of the AppCommander-wide doctrine shift consolidating five comms files to one and reducing each spawn's runtime dependency on AppCommander. The five-file bundle was structurally heavy for what it represented (point-in-time session state + flushed event log + dual-audience narratives + operational handoff), and the deferred-flush rule meant every session ended by writing five artifacts in one batch. The new shape is honest about what the artifact is — a single JSON file that the next session reads, the current session overwrites, the close hook archives + commits + pushes. Same loop, fewer files, no per-event append discipline to maintain. See AppCommander's COMMS_V2_AND_ADMIN_PAGE_SHIFT.md for full context. The dispatch-sandbox-mode hook adjustment ships here as a project-local patch; if other spawns also run under PFOR-016-style sandbox mode, the same patch should ride into the AppCommander-side template so every spawn inherits a working loop.

The session-close.sh hook as templated assumed the carpenter is checked out on main; under PFOR-016 dispatch-sandbox mode (carpenter works on a branch, pushes to main via 'git push origin <branch>:main') its push silently failed and produced an infinite Stop-fire loop when combined with this repo's pre-existing branch-gate hook. Recommend lifting this branch-detection logic into the AppCommander-side template if other spawns run under similar sandbox modes.
